dog.description_text:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Leonite is on the at-risk list due to behavior. He is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. He has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to his stress levels, it is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give him plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

A volunteer writes: Eight month old Leonite, a cute young Tabby was brought to the care center as he did not live to his new owner's expectations. That happens and nobody is at fault...Nothing is known about Leonite 's past but being a very shy youngster, we can imagine that he might not have been very much socialized, explaining why he likes to stay in hiding and avoid interactions with people. Lately, though, Leonite stays in his main kennel area, lounging on his kuranda bed, accepting petting on his head and back with a feather, slow blinking at me when I speak softly to him and playing actively with a feather wand(see video). It is progress. Nothing happens overnight...We are hoping for more steps forward and eventually seeing Leonite going home with an experienced and patient mew owner, in a quiet home without boisterous children. Leonide is a youngster who needs to be given a chance at being a beloved and loving pet. He is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center!
dog.name: Leonite
